content: Dimples are visible indentations on the skin that appear on some individuals' cheeks when they smile. These indentations are caused by the underlying structure of the flesh and are inherited genetically as a dominant trait. It is relatively common for individuals with dimples to have them on both cheeks. However, a less common variation is the presence of a single dimple, which appears on only one side of the face. From an anatomical perspective, dimples are thought to result from variations in the structure of the zygomaticus major muscle, a facial muscle involved in smiling. Specifically, the presence of a bifid, or double, zygomaticus major muscle may explain the formation of cheek dimples. This bifid muscle originates as a single structure from the zygomatic bone. As it extends forward (anteriorly), it divides into two separate bundles. The superior bundle attaches above the corner of the mouth, while the inferior bundle attaches below the corner of the mouth. In some cultures, dimples are regarded as a feature of physical attractiveness. Dimples are also commonly observed in infants, but they may diminish or become less noticeable over time as the facial muscles elongate with age. For this reason, dimples are often associated with youthfulness.
